stem:
Parul's class asks why the Northern Hemisphere has summer in June while the Southern Hemisphere has winter then.

Which reason is correct?

options.text: Earth's tilted axis stays pointed the same way as Earth revolves, so in June the Northern Hemisphere gets more direct sunlight and longer days.
In June the Northern Hemisphere is closer to the Sun because of the tilt.
In June the Northern Hemisphere has winter.
In June both hemispheres have summer.

teacher.key_rationale: Seasons come from the maintained tilt as Earth revolves, changing sunlight and day length by hemisphere. Closer-to-Sun from tilt confuses distance with angle. June winter reverses the season. Both hemispheres do not share summer in June.
